title: Desired state and Current state, and the new / existing mark on every feature
subtitle: Detailed › Baseline becomes Desired state (the left menu item too) (what the product should become); a new Current state holds what runs today, with proof. Every feature carries one mark: New, In progress or Exists. Invented data: 60 features, 10 exist (one with old proof), 6 in progress, 44 new.

decisions.name: How Current state is shown and kept true
decisions.question: How should Current state show what runs today, and what does an item with old or missing proof look like?
decisions.common: A Current state tab beside Desired state in Detailed. Each built feature lists its proof: code map files, merged pull requests, tracker tasks done and a measured value, read by Oracle each night. The owner confirms. The one feature whose proof is 41 days old (Invoices as PDF) stands out and can be checked again. In Detailed the left menu item Baseline is renamed Desired state.

proposals.name: Proof table
proposals.what: One table: each running feature on a row with when it shipped, its four kinds of proof and when the proof was last checked. Rows with old proof sort to the top in amber with a Check again button; checking opens a short list under the row where Oracle re-reads each proof and the owner answers Yes, still runs / Changed / No longer runs.
proposals.why: It answers 'what runs today and can I trust it' in one scan, scales to dozens of features without new screens, and puts the owner's confirm right where the doubt is.
proposals.plus: Everything comparable side by side; old proof is impossible to miss; check happens in place.
proposals.cost: A wide table: on a phone each row stacks to three lines and the measured value is dropped.

frames.caption: At rest: 10 running features, the one with old proof first, in amber with Check again.
Check again opened under the row: the four proofs Oracle will re-read, and the owner's three answers.
Mid-check: three proofs re-read and still true; the measured value for October is not in yet.
The result: the owner said Yes, still runs; the row reads Checked Nov 3 · you confirmed and the top says 0 with old proof.
Hard case at 1512: the 10 running features with Check again in full beside the Ask rail, and the 50 still in Desired state (6 in progress, 44 new) below.
Phone 390, dark: each row stacks name, date, proof and freshness; the check opens under the row.

proposals.name: Cards by area
proposals.what: Current state is grouped by area of focus: one card per area, each running feature with a freshness bar that shortens as its proof ages. Old proof gets a dashed amber border. Opening a feature shows a side panel with its proof, newest first, and the owner's confirm.
proposals.plus: Shows at a glance which areas are thin or empty today; freshness reads as a picture.
proposals.cost: Proof details are hidden until a feature is opened; with 10 features half the cards are near empty and the side panel takes about a quarter of the width.

frames.caption: At rest: six area cards; Invoices as PDF has a dashed amber border and a short bar.
Invoices as PDF opened: the side panel shows its proof, newest first, with Check it now.
Mid-check: the owner picks Still runs as before, about to confirm.
The result: the card is solid again, Checked Nov 3 · you confirmed; the top says 0 with old proof.
Hard case at 1512: cards with 1 or 2 features each, plus the 50 still in Desired state below.
Phone 390, dark: the cards stack in one column; the side panel does not fit on a phone, so the proof history is not shown here.

proposals.name: Shipped timeline
proposals.what: Current state reads as a dated list, newest first, grouped by month: each entry says when it shipped and its proof. An entry with old proof turns grey with a dashed line and an Ask its owner link, which sends the owner of that feature a question; their answer refreshes the proof.
proposals.plus: Reads like release notes; the person who knows answers, not only the product owner.
proposals.cost: Old features sink to the bottom, so the stale one (May) is found by scrolling; waiting for a person can take days.

frames.caption: At rest: entries by month; Invoices as PDF (May) is amber, dashed, with Not checked since Sep 23.
Scrolled down to May: Ask Lena Fischbach opened under Invoices as PDF, with a prefilled question and Send.
Mid: asked Nov 3, 9:12 AM, waiting for an answer.
The result: Lena Fischbach confirmed Nov 3; the proof line now reads 3,520 sent in October, and the top says 0 with old proof.
Hard case at 1512: the full list with the 50 still in Desired state below.
Phone 390, dark, scrolled to May: the stale entry hides its proof line to fit; the ask box opens under it.

decisions.name: The new / in progress / exists mark
decisions.question: How should every feature show whether it is new, in progress or already exists?
decisions.common: One mark per feature, with three states: New (asked for or planned, nothing built), In progress (being built) and Exists (runs today, with proof); Exists with old proof is told apart. Shown on Simple › Priorities, with a Show filter that counts each kind; the same mark goes on roadmap bars, one-pager lines, Ask Oracle answers, meeting agenda items and Home (the places frames show four of them). Clicking a mark says what it means and its proof. Each feature has its own code.

proposals.name: Shape plus word
proposals.what: A small circle whose fill tells the stage (dashed and empty = New, half filled = In progress, filled with a tick = Exists, filled with ! = Exists with old proof) plus the word beside it. Where room is tight (a roadmap bar, a phone row, a chat line) the circle stays and the word goes to the hover text.
proposals.why: The shape works without colour and at any size, so one mark can live on a bar and in a sentence; the word removes guessing where there is room.
proposals.plus: Readable in light, dark and for colour-blind readers; one look from bar to chat.
proposals.cost: Three shapes to learn; on the smallest spots only the shape shows.

frames.caption: At rest: Priorities with the Show filter (All 60 · New 44 · In progress 6 · Exists 10) and a mark on every row.
The first row's mark opened: what In progress means and its proof so far.
Mid: the owner presses New in the Show filter.
The result: only the 44 new features, ranks kept.
Hard case at 1512: all 60 ranked features, the old-proof one marked Exists · proof old.
Phone 390, dark: the shape and word fit beside the code on each row.

The mark in four other places, side by side: a Billing roadmap bar, a one-pager line, an Ask Oracle answer and a meeting agenda item. On a roadmap bar the word is dropped and only the shape shows; in a sentence the word reads well.
Phone 390, dark: the roadmap bars and the one-pager line.
Phone 390, dark, scrolled on: the Ask Oracle answer and the agenda item.

proposals.name: Word pill
proposals.what: A coloured pill with the word in capitals: NEW (blue), IN PROGRESS (amber), EXISTS (green), EXISTS · PROOF OLD (amber). No shapes to learn.
proposals.plus: Nothing to decode; obvious in a meeting agenda or an export.
proposals.cost: Wide: on a phone it pushes the title to its own line, and on a roadmap bar it does not fit at all; leans on colour for the old-proof case.

frames.caption: At rest: pills on every row and in the Show filter.
The first row's pill opened: what In progress means and its proof.
Mid: pressing NEW in the Show filter.
The result: only the 44 new features.
Hard case at 1512: 60 rows; the pills differ in width, so the titles after them start at different places.
Phone 390, dark: the pill pushes the title onto its own line on every row.

The mark in four other places, side by side: a Billing roadmap bar, a one-pager line, an Ask Oracle answer and a meeting agenda item. On a roadmap bar the pill leaves almost no room, so short bars show just 'Yea…'; in sentences it reads well.
Phone 390, dark: the roadmap bars and the one-pager line.
Phone 390, dark, scrolled on: the Ask Oracle answer and the agenda item.

proposals.name: Edge stripe
proposals.what: A thin vertical stripe before the name: outlined = New, half filled = In progress, solid = Exists, striped = Exists with old proof. The word only shows on hover and in the Show filter.
proposals.plus: Takes almost no room; rows stay calm with 44 new features.
proposals.cost: Too subtle to read without the legend; does not work inside a sentence (chat answers, agendas).

frames.caption: At rest: a thin stripe before every name; the Show filter is the legend.
The first row's stripe opened: what In progress means and its proof.
Mid: pressing New in the Show filter.
The result: only the 44 new features.
Hard case at 1512: 60 rows; the old-proof stripe is hard to spot among the others.
Phone 390, dark: stripes fit, but the meaning lives only in the filter at the top.

The mark in four other places, side by side: a Billing roadmap bar, a one-pager line, an Ask Oracle answer and a meeting agenda item. In a sentence the stripe reads as a stray bar with no meaning; on a roadmap bar it fits well.
Phone 390, dark: the roadmap bars and the one-pager line.
Phone 390, dark, scrolled on: the Ask Oracle answer and the agenda item.

decisions.name: How a feature moves to Current state
decisions.question: When a feature ships with proof, should it move to Current state on its own with an undo, or should the owner confirm each move?
decisions.common: Oracle notices proof is in (code map, merged pull requests, all tracker tasks done, a measured value). The feature then leaves Desired state and joins Current state, where a note says when and how it moved. Here: Saved searches and Retry failed payments have their proof in.

proposals.name: Moves on proof
proposals.what: As soon as the proof is in, Oracle moves the feature itself and says so with a message that has Undo. Undo puts it back in Desired state as In progress.
proposals.plus: No work for the owner; Current state is never behind.
proposals.cost: A wrong reading (a merged pull request that was turned off) moves a feature that does not run; several moves overnight arrive as one message that is easy to miss.

frames.caption: At rest: Desired state; Saved searches says Proof is in.
Saved searches moved by itself: it leaves the list (Desired state 49, Current state 11), and the message offers Undo and See proof.
Mid: the owner pressed Undo and is asked to confirm it; Saved searches is still out of the list until they say yes.
The result after keeping it: Current state (11) lists Saved searches, Moved today on proof.
Hard case at 1512: two moved overnight in one message; both are gone from the 48 left in Desired state, Current state reads 12.
Phone 390, dark: the message spans the width just above the tab bar and wraps to two lines; Undo is the only way to see what moved.

proposals.name: Owner confirms each
proposals.what: Features whose proof is in gather in a Ready to move band at the top of Desired state. Opening one shows its proof; Move to Current state moves it, Not yet keeps it. Nothing moves without the owner's yes.
proposals.why: The owner asked to confirm what runs; one click per feature with the proof in front of them keeps Current state trustworthy, and a ready band is easy to clear.
proposals.plus: Every move is checked by a person; the proof is shown at the moment of the decision.
proposals.cost: One click per feature; if the owner is away, ready features wait in Desired state.

frames.caption: At rest: Ready to move · 2 at the top of Desired state.
Saved searches opened: its four proofs and Move to Current state.
Mid: Move pressed, moving.
The result: Current state (11) lists Saved searches, Moved Nov 3 · you confirmed; Desired state reads 49.
Hard case at 1512: only the 2 with proof sit in the band, each needs a yes; the other 4 in progress stay in the list of 50 with their tasks left.
Phone 390, dark: the proof opens over the list; the band wraps to two lines.

proposals.name: Friday check
proposals.what: Once a week Oracle lists what may have shipped. The owner ticks the ones that did and moves them together; the rest stay with a reason.
proposals.plus: One short session a week; good for a weekly review meeting.
proposals.cost: Current state can be up to a week behind; a long list invites ticking everything.

frames.caption: At rest: the Friday check banner, 3 features may have shipped.
Review opened: three features with their proof, none ticked yet.
Mid: two ticked; Report builder has 5 tasks open and stays.
The result: Current state (12) shows 2 moved, 1 left in Desired state (48) with why.
Hard case at 1512: 6 features to review at once above 50 in Desired state.
Phone 390, dark: the review list fills the screen under the banner.
